title: Universality of dimensional crossovers in topological insulators
authors: Lumen Eek, Zeb Osseweijer, Cristiane Morais Smith
abstract: We investigate dimensional crossovers in minimal tight-binding models of three-dimensional (3D) topological insulators subject to geometric confinement. While thin films are commonly understood to host a crossover from a 3D strong topological insulator to a two-dimensional (2D) quantum spin Hall phase via hybridization of surface states, we demonstrate that this picture is incomplete once bulk confinement effects and boundary termination are fully taken into account. Using lattice models, we show that reducing the system size induces a strongly non-monotonic dependence of the topology on thickness and microscopic parameters, leading to a sequence of topological phase transitions that is highly sensitive to surface termination. In particular, we find a cascade of dimensional reduction from a 3D topological insulator to a 2D quantum spin Hall phase and ultimately to a one-dimensional phase consisting of end states of Kramers pairs protected by inversion symmetry. Remarkably, we show that both the 2D and 1D topological phases can emerge even when the corresponding 3D bulk phase is topologically trivial. Our results reveal an unexpected universality in the phase diagrams of 3D-to-2D and 2D-to-1D crossovers, pointing toward a unified framework for topology under dimensional reduction.
summary: This work explores how topological insulators behave under geometric confinement, moving from 3D bulk materials down to 1D edge states. By analyzing lattice models, the authors demonstrate a universal sequence of phase transitions governed by dimensionality reduction. This reveals that topology can be robustly maintained or induced at boundaries even if the original material was not intrinsically topological.
main_problem: The study investigates dimensional crossovers in topological insulators (TIs) when subjected to geometric confinement, showing that simple surface state hybridization models are incomplete.
main_result: A cascade of topological transitions occurs (3DTI $	o$ 2D QSH $	o$ 1D phase), revealing an unexpected universality in the phase diagrams across these dimensional reductions. Furthermore, lower-dimensional phases can emerge even if the parent 3D bulk material is topologically trivial.
method: The authors use lattice models and calculate topological invariants ($\mathbb{Z}_2$) using methods like the Fu-Kane formula and the Wilson-loop method to analyze slab and rod spectra.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by minimal tight-binding Hamiltonians for 3D TIs on a cubic lattice, analyzed under geometric confinement (thin films/slabs) terminated along [100], [110], or [111] directions.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on lattice models and specific symmetry considerations (Time-Reversal Symmetry, Inversion Symmetry).

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the transition from 3D to 2D QSH phases using Wilson loops, then extends this analysis to 1D end states. It establishes universal patterns governing these dimensional reductions by comparing results across different terminations.
why_interesting: The concept of topological protection persisting or emerging in lower dimensions, even when the bulk is trivial, provides a powerful framework for understanding material design and boundary effects relevant to quantum devices.
